meta.title: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum
meta.deck: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum
sents.zh: 棘手的局面：新加坡为什么至今还不卖口香糖给你
notes: a sticky situation：棘手的局面。sticky 本义是“黏的”，和口香糖一语双关。
won't sell you ...：不肯卖给你……。

sents.en: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.
sents.zh: 禁止这东西三十多年后，这个城市国家仍然丝毫没有松口的迹象。
notes: the stuff：那东西，口语地指口香糖。
city-state：城市国家（如新加坡）。
show little sign of doing：几乎没有……的迹象。relent：让步、松口。

sents.en: Visitors find the rule baffling; many locals barely notice it.
sents.zh: 游客觉得这条规定莫名其妙；很多本地人却几乎注意不到它。
notes: find sth + 形容词：觉得……怎样。
baffling：令人困惑的。
分号前后对比：游客 vs 本地人。

sents.en: In 1992 Singapore made it illegal to import or sell chewing gum, a law that still raises eyebrows abroad.
sents.zh: 1992 年，新加坡规定进口或销售口香糖都是违法的，这条法律至今仍让外国人惊讶。
notes: made it illegal to ...：使……成为违法，it 是形式宾语。
a law that ...：同位语，补充说明。
raise eyebrows：引起惊讶或不满。

sents.en: The government's reasoning was practical rather than moral.
sents.zh: 政府的理由是出于实际，而不是出于道德。
notes: reasoning：理由、推理。
practical rather than moral：是实际的，而不是道德的。

sents.en: Cleaners were spending a fortune scraping gum off pavements, stairwells and lift buttons.
sents.zh: 清洁工花了大笔钱，从人行道、楼梯间和电梯按钮上刮口香糖。
notes: spend a fortune doing：花一大笔钱做……。
scrape A off B：把 A 从 B 上刮下来。
pavement、lift 是英式说法（美式 sidewalk、elevator）。

sents.en: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.
sents.zh: 据大多数说法，压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，是有人搞破坏，把口香糖粘在新地铁列车的车门感应器上，导致车门卡住、列车停运。
notes: the last straw：压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。
according to most accounts：据大多数说法。
causing doors to jam and services to stall：导致……，现在分词表结果。

sents.en: Singapore had a reputation to protect.
sents.zh: 新加坡有自己的名声要维护。
notes: a reputation to protect：要维护的名声，不定式作定语。

sents.en: Since independence it has prided itself on being clean, green and orderly, and its leaders have never been shy about regulating daily life to keep it that way.
sents.zh: 独立以来，新加坡一直以干净、绿化好、秩序井然为荣，它的领导人也从不避讳通过规管日常生活来保持这种状态。
notes: pride oneself on：以……为荣。
orderly：整齐的、有秩序的。
be shy about doing：对做……有顾虑，never been shy about = 毫不避讳。

sents.en: Fines for littering, spitting and failing to flush public toilets have long been part of the deal.
sents.zh: 乱扔垃圾、随地吐痰、上完公厕不冲水都会被罚款，这一直是这份“约定”的一部分。
notes: Fines for ...：对……的罚款。
littering, spitting and failing to flush：三个动名词并列。
part of the deal：交易的一部分，这里指“生活在这里就得接受的规矩”。

sents.en: To outsiders, such rules can look like a nanny state at its most fussy.
sents.zh: 在外人看来，这些规定像是“保姆式国家”管得最琐碎的样子。
notes: nanny state：保姆式国家，指政府管得太多。
at its most fussy：在它最挑剔、最琐碎的时候。

sents.en: Many residents are unbothered.
sents.zh: 很多居民对此毫不在意。
notes: unbothered：不在意的、不受困扰的。

sents.en: They point out that the streets are spotless and the trains run smoothly, and that nobody is being asked to sacrifice more than a minor pleasure.
sents.zh: 他们指出，街道一尘不染，地铁运行顺畅，而且没有人需要牺牲的不过是一点小小的乐趣。
notes: point out that ...：指出……，后面两个 that 从句并列。
spotless：一尘不染的。
sacrifice more than a minor pleasure：牺牲的不过是小乐趣。

sents.en: Since 2004, under a trade deal with America, pharmacies have been allowed to sell gum with health benefits, such as nicotine gum for smokers trying to quit.
sents.zh: 从 2004 年起，根据和美国的一项贸易协议，药房获准出售有保健作用的口香糖，比如给想戒烟的人用的尼古丁口香糖。
notes: under a trade deal：根据一项贸易协议。
have been allowed to：获准……。
smokers trying to quit：想戒烟的人。quit = 戒掉、放弃。

sents.en: Buyers were at first required to leave their names with the pharmacist.
sents.zh: 起初，购买者还得在药剂师那里登记姓名。
notes: at first：起初。
were required to：被要求……。

sents.en: A persistent myth holds that chewing gum in Singapore can get you caned.
sents.zh: 有一个流传不衰的说法：在新加坡嚼口香糖会被鞭刑。
notes: persistent：持续存在的、顽固的。
myth：（错误的）说法、迷思。
hold that ...：认为……（这里指“这个说法认为”）。

sents.en: It cannot; the famous caning of an American teenager in 1994 was for vandalising cars, not for gum.
sents.zh: 并不会；1994 年那起著名的美国少年被鞭刑事件，是因为他破坏汽车，而不是因为口香糖。
notes: It cannot：并不能（会）。
was for vandalising cars：是因为破坏汽车。

sents.en: But the myth survives because it fits a wider story about a strict little country that likes to keep order.
sents.zh: 但这个说法之所以流传下来，是因为它符合一个更大的故事：一个喜欢维持秩序的严格小国。
notes: fit：符合、吻合。
a wider story about ...：关于……的更大叙事。
that likes to keep order：定语从句修饰 country。

sents.en: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.
sents.zh: 就新加坡人自己而言，他们对这条禁令往往是带着几分好笑的漠不关心。
notes: for their part：就他们而言。
treat ... with ...：以……态度对待……。
amused indifference：觉得好笑又不在乎。

sents.en: Some joke that the first thing they buy on holiday abroad is a packet of gum.
sents.zh: 有人开玩笑说，他们出国度假买的第一样东西就是一包口香糖。
notes: joke that ...：开玩笑说。on holiday abroad：出国度假时。

sents.en: Others say they have simply lost the habit.
sents.zh: 也有人说，他们干脆已经没这个习惯了。
notes: lose the habit：失去某个习惯、戒掉某个习惯。

sents.en: Either way, the gum has not come back, and neither has the mess.
sents.zh: 不管怎样，口香糖没有回来，那些脏乱也没有回来。
notes: Either way：不管怎样。
neither has the mess：……也没有（回来）。neither 后面倒装：助动词 has 放在主语前。

sents.en: In Singapore, at least, some problems stay solved because nobody is allowed to chew on them.
sents.zh: 至少在新加坡，有些问题一直不再出现，因为谁也不准再“嚼”它们。
notes: stay solved：保持已解决的状态。
chew on：本义“嚼”，引申为“仔细琢磨”，这里一语双关作结。

vocab.zh: 棘手的局面、尴尬的处境
vocab.note: sticky 本义“黏的”，引申为“棘手的、难办的”：a sticky problem（棘手的问题）。

ex.en: Forgetting her name put me in a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 忘了她的名字让我很尴尬。

ex.en: He talked his way out of a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 他靠一张嘴摆脱了困境。

vocab.note: 一个城市就是一个国家：Singapore and Monaco are city-states. 古希腊的雅典也是城邦（city-state）。

ex.en: Singapore is a small but wealthy [[city-state]].
ex.zh: 新加坡是个小而富裕的城市国家。

ex.en: Ancient Athens was a powerful [[city-state]].
ex.zh: 古代雅典是一个强大的城邦。

vocab.note: show no / little sign of doing sth：The rain showed no sign of stopping.（雨丝毫没有要停的意思。）

ex.en: The rain [[showed no sign of]] stopping.
ex.zh: 雨丝毫没有要停的意思。

ex.en: Prices [[show little sign of]] falling.
ex.zh: 价格几乎没有下降的迹象。

vocab.note: 原本坚持的态度软化：Her parents finally relented.（她父母最终让步了。）形容词 relentless（毫不留情的）。

ex.en: Her parents finally [[relented]] and let her go.
ex.zh: 她父母最终松口，让她去了。

ex.en: The storm showed no sign of [[relenting]].
ex.zh: 暴风雨丝毫没有减弱的迹象。

vocab.zh: 令人费解的、莫名其妙的
vocab.note: baffle（使困惑）+ -ing。I find it baffling that ...（我搞不懂为什么……）

ex.en: The instructions were completely [[baffling]].
ex.zh: 说明书完全看不懂。

ex.en: Doctors were [[baffled]] by her illness.
ex.zh: 医生们对她的病情感到困惑。

vocab.note: 挑起眉毛表示惊讶或不赞同：His decision raised a few eyebrows.（他的决定让一些人很惊讶。）

ex.en: Her bright green hair [[raised eyebrows]] at the office.
ex.zh: 她那头亮绿色的头发在办公室引人侧目。

ex.en: The price [[raised a few eyebrows]].
ex.zh: 这个价格让一些人吃了一惊。

vocab.note: the reasoning behind a decision（某个决定背后的理由）。动词 reason（推理）。

ex.en: I don't understand the [[reasoning]] behind this rule.
ex.zh: 我不明白这条规定背后的道理。

ex.en: Her [[reasoning]] was simple: it's too expensive.
ex.zh: 她的理由很简单：太贵了。

vocab.note: fortune 是“财富、一大笔钱”。cost a fortune（贵得要命），make a fortune（发大财）。

ex.en: They [[spent a fortune]] on the wedding.
ex.zh: 他们在婚礼上花了一大笔钱。

ex.en: That coat must have [[cost a fortune]].
ex.zh: 那件外套一定贵得要命。

vocab.note: scrape A off B：scrape ice off the windscreen（把挡风玻璃上的冰刮掉）。也说 scrape off sth。

ex.en: He [[scraped off]] the old paint.
ex.zh: 他把旧漆刮掉了。

ex.en: I spent ten minutes [[scraping off]] the ice.
ex.zh: 我花了十分钟把冰刮掉。

vocab.note: 楼里装楼梯的竖井空间。staircase 是楼梯本身。

ex.en: The kids played in the [[stairwell]].
ex.zh: 孩子们在楼梯间里玩。

ex.en: The [[stairwell]] was dark and cold.
ex.zh: 楼梯间又黑又冷。

vocab.zh: 压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草、忍无可忍
vocab.note: 来自谚语 the straw that broke the camel's back。That's the last straw!（我受够了！）

ex.en: Being late again was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 又迟到，这让人忍无可忍了。

ex.en: When the TV broke, that was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 电视坏了，这成了压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

vocab.note: account 在这里是“叙述、说法”。by all accounts：大家都说。

ex.en: [[By all accounts]], she is a brilliant teacher.
ex.zh: 大家都说她是个出色的老师。

ex.en: [[According to most accounts]], the fire started in the kitchen.
ex.zh: 据大多数说法，火是从厨房烧起来的。

vocab.note: 动词 vandalise（故意破坏），名词 vandalism（破坏公物的行为）。

ex.en: [[Vandals]] smashed the bus shelter.
ex.zh: 有人把公交候车亭砸了。

ex.en: The statue was [[vandalised]] overnight.
ex.zh: 雕像一夜之间被人破坏了。

vocab.note: The car stalled.（车熄火了。）The talks stalled.（谈判陷入僵局。）

ex.en: The car [[stalled]] at the traffic lights.
ex.zh: 车在红绿灯前熄火了。

ex.en: Peace talks have [[stalled]] again.
ex.zh: 和谈再次陷入僵局。

vocab.note: a good / bad reputation，have a reputation for（以……出名）。动词 repute 不常用。

ex.en: The restaurant has a [[reputation]] for great fish.
ex.zh: 这家餐厅以鱼做得好而出名。

ex.en: One mistake can ruin your [[reputation]].
ex.zh: 一个错误就可能毁了你的名声。

vocab.note: pride 作动词只用于这个结构：She prides herself on her cooking.（她对自己的厨艺很自豪。）

ex.en: The hotel [[prides itself on]] its service.
ex.zh: 这家酒店以服务为傲。

ex.en: She [[prides herself on]] never being late.
ex.zh: 她以从不迟到为荣。

vocab.note: an orderly queue（排得整整齐齐的队），in an orderly way（有条不紊地）。注意 -ly 结尾但它是形容词。

ex.en: Please leave the building in an [[orderly]] way.
ex.zh: 请有序地离开大楼。

ex.en: Her desk is always neat and [[orderly]].
ex.zh: 她的桌子总是整整齐齐。

vocab.note: 用规则管控：regulate the use of drones（规范无人机的使用）。名词 regulation（规定）。

ex.en: The government plans to [[regulate]] online games.
ex.zh: 政府计划规范网络游戏。

ex.en: Sweat helps [[regulate]] body temperature.
ex.zh: 出汗有助于调节体温。

vocab.note: 动词：Don't litter.（别乱扔垃圾。）名词：pick up litter（捡垃圾）。

ex.en: You can be fined for [[littering]].
ex.zh: 乱扔垃圾会被罚款。

ex.en: The beach was covered in [[litter]].
ex.zh: 沙滩上满是垃圾。

vocab.note: 过去式 spat（英式也用 spit）。spit out：吐出来。

ex.en: Please don't [[spit]] on the street.
ex.zh: 请不要随地吐痰。

ex.en: The baby [[spat]] out the medicine.
ex.zh: 宝宝把药吐了出来。

vocab.note: flush the toilet（冲马桶）。也指脸红：She flushed with anger.

ex.en: Remember to [[flush]] the toilet.
ex.zh: 记得冲马桶。

ex.en: Something is wrong — the toilet won't [[flush]].
ex.zh: 马桶坏了，冲不下去。

vocab.note: Long hours are part of the deal.（工作时间长是这份工作的一部分，没办法。）

ex.en: Working weekends is [[part of the deal]].
ex.zh: 周末加班是这份工作的一部分。

ex.en: Crowds are [[part of the deal]] when you visit Paris.
ex.zh: 去巴黎就得接受人多。

vocab.zh: 保姆式国家（管得太多的政府）
vocab.note: 贬义，批评政府什么都管：Critics call the smoking ban an example of the nanny state.

ex.en: Some people call the new rules the [[nanny state]] gone mad.
ex.zh: 有人说新规定是保姆式国家管疯了。

ex.en: He hates the idea of a [[nanny state]].
ex.zh: 他讨厌政府什么都管。

vocab.zh: 挑剔的、过分讲究的；琐碎的
vocab.note: a fussy eater（挑食的人）。not fussy：无所谓、不挑。

ex.en: My son is a very [[fussy]] eater.
ex.zh: 我儿子特别挑食。

ex.en: I'm not [[fussy]] — any restaurant is fine.
ex.zh: 我不挑，哪家餐厅都行。

vocab.note: un-（不）+ bothered（被打扰的）。口语也说 I'm not bothered.（我无所谓。）

ex.en: She seemed [[unbothered]] by the rain.
ex.zh: 她似乎一点也不在意下雨。

ex.en: He stayed calm and [[unbothered]].
ex.zh: 他保持冷静，毫不在意。

vocab.note: point out that ... / point sth out：He pointed out a mistake.（他指出了一个错误。）

ex.en: She [[pointed out]] a mistake in my essay.
ex.zh: 她指出了我文章里的一个错误。

ex.en: Experts [[point out]] that the risk is small.
ex.zh: 专家指出风险很小。

vocab.zh: 一尘不染的、非常干净的
vocab.note: spot（污点）+ -less（没有）。a spotless kitchen / record（干净的厨房 / 清白的记录）。

ex.en: The hotel room was [[spotless]].
ex.zh: 酒店房间一尘不染。

ex.en: He has a [[spotless]] driving record.
ex.zh: 他的驾驶记录毫无污点。

vocab.note: a trade deal between two countries。free trade agreement：自由贸易协定。

ex.en: The two countries signed a new [[trade deal]].
ex.zh: 两国签了一项新的贸易协议。

ex.en: Farmers hope the [[trade deal]] will help them.
ex.zh: 农民希望这项贸易协议能帮到他们。

vocab.note: 英式也说 chemist's，美式也说 drugstore。pharmacist：药剂师。

ex.en: Is there a [[pharmacy]] near here?
ex.zh: 附近有药店吗？

ex.en: You can buy it at any [[pharmacy]].
ex.zh: 任何药店都能买到。

vocab.note: quit smoking（戒烟），quit one's job（辞职）。过去式和过去分词都是 quit。

ex.en: He [[quit]] smoking last year.
ex.zh: 他去年戒了烟。

ex.en: She decided to [[quit]] her job.
ex.zh: 她决定辞职。

vocab.zh: 持续的、顽固的；坚持不懈的
vocab.note: a persistent cough（久咳不愈），a persistent salesman（死缠烂打的推销员）。名词 persistence。

ex.en: I've had a [[persistent]] cough for weeks.
ex.zh: 我咳嗽了好几周都不好。

ex.en: Her [[persistent]] questions finally got an answer.
ex.zh: 她不停追问，终于得到了答复。

vocab.note: It's a myth that ...：……是个误区。Greek myths（希腊神话）。

ex.en: It's a [[myth]] that goldfish forget everything in seconds.
ex.zh: 金鱼几秒钟就忘事，这是个误区。

ex.en: She loves reading Greek [[myths]].
ex.zh: 她爱读希腊神话。

vocab.note: fit the description（符合描述），fit the facts（与事实相符）。

ex.en: He [[fits]] the description of the thief.
ex.zh: 他符合小偷的特征。

ex.en: Your idea doesn't [[fit]] the facts.
ex.zh: 你的想法和事实对不上。

vocab.note: for my part（就我而言），for their part（就他们而言）。用来引出某一方的态度。

ex.en: [[For my part]], I'm happy to wait.
ex.zh: 就我而言，我很乐意等。

ex.en: The company, [[for its part]], denies everything.
ex.zh: 公司方面则否认一切。

vocab.note: 形容词 indifferent（漠不关心的）。with indifference：冷淡地。

ex.en: He listened with complete [[indifference]].
ex.zh: 他听着，完全无动于衷。

ex.en: She was [[indifferent]] to the news.
ex.zh: 她对这个消息漠不关心。

vocab.note: 也说 get out of the habit of doing。反义 get into the habit（养成习惯）。

ex.en: I've [[lost the habit]] of reading before bed.
ex.zh: 我已经不再睡前看书了。

ex.en: Try not to [[get out of the habit]] of exercising.
ex.zh: 尽量别丢了锻炼的习惯。

vocab.expr: neither + 助动词 + 主语（倒装）
vocab.note: 前面是否定句，接“……也不”时用 neither / nor + 助动词 + 主语：I can't swim, and neither can my sister.（我不会游泳，我妹妹也不会。）肯定句用 so：I like tea, and so does she.

ex.en: I haven't seen it, and [[neither has]] Tom.
ex.zh: 我没看过，汤姆也没看过。

ex.en: She loves jazz, and [[so does]] her husband.
ex.zh: 她爱爵士乐，她丈夫也爱。

vocab.conn: 否定句, and neither + 助动词 + 主语（肯定句用 so + 助动词 + 主语）
vocab.say: the gum has not come back, and neither has the mess

pick.q: I don't like horror films, and neither ___ my brother.
pick.why: 前句用 don't（do 的否定），接 neither 时用同一个助动词：neither does。

pick.q: She can speak French, and ___ can her son.
pick.why: 前句是肯定句（can speak），“也会”用 so can her son。

vocab.note: chew on a pencil（咬铅笔）。比喻：Let me chew on it for a day.（让我琢磨一天。）

ex.en: The dog likes to [[chew on]] my shoes.
ex.zh: 那只狗喜欢啃我的鞋。

ex.en: Give me a day to [[chew on]] your offer.
ex.zh: 给我一天时间琢磨你的提议。

cloze.hint: 几乎没有……的迹象（shows little ___ of）
据大多数说法（according to most ___）
（不得不接受的）一部分（part of the ___）

breakdown.en: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.
points: 主干：The last straw ... came when ... —— 最后一根稻草出现在……的时候。
according to most accounts：插入语，“据大多数说法”。
when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains：时间状语从句，说明发生了什么。
causing doors to jam and services to stall：现在分词短语表示结果，cause sth to do = 导致……。
